rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both are short international communications organized around disaster-caused suffering, American assistance that alleviated that suffering, and the President's gratification shared with the American people. The close verbal correspondences—especially “suffering caused,” “assistance,” “alleviate,” “gratification,” and “American people”—are distinctive and material. C10 shares the disaster-relief subject and a thankful response to a prior letter, while C05 shares assistance-related satisfaction, but neither approaches C01's combined linguistic and structural fit.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The American people were deeply moved by the reports of the suffering caused by the prolonged drought and the recent disastrous floods.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I wish to express to you in the name of the Government and the people of the United States our deep sympathy for the suffering caused to so many of the Italian people
shared_material.explanation: Both foreground national sympathy for suffering caused by a natural disaster.

shared_material.child_excerpt: our food and assistance were timely and did much to alleviate the intense hardship caused by these disasters
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whatever assistance United States forces, stationed in Italy, may have been able to provide to alleviate this suffering
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive assistance-to-alleviate-suffering construction is closely preserved and adapted to different disasters and aid.

shared_material.child_excerpt: We are most happy to know that our food and assistance were timely
shared_material.parent_excerpt: is a matter of gratification to me and to the American people
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude the substantive message by expressing presidential and public satisfaction that American assistance helped.
